page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by custom 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton processors, specifically the Neoverse-N1 model. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz with a dedicated CPU allocation and no hyperthreading. The processor configuration includes 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per core.

This instance is bundled with 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, providing high-speed, low-latency local instance store volumes. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps. The underlying virtualization is managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, ensuring minimal overhead and secure isolation.

Performance benchmarks place the c6gd.8xlarge in the average tier for most multi-core and database operations. It achieves a multi-core stress-ng score of 48571.1 and a Passmark CPU score of 17314.07. Database performance is solid, with Redis SET operations reaching 40.61 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring 20441.91. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 958.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 20.31 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient for small cached blocks at 1894.03 GB/sec, but drops to 173.34 GB/sec for larger uncached blocks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture delivers a high density of physical cores and local NVMe storage without the premium associated with traditional x86 architectures. This makes the instance highly suitable for multi-threaded workloads that benefit from local scratch space, such as software compilation, static web serving, and distributed database nodes. It is also capable of handling moderate machine learning tasks, processing 7B parameter LLM prompts at 31.97 tokens per second.

Benchmarks indicate average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 48571.1 and strong database capabilities, including 40.61 million Redis SET operations per second.
